'''Yuan-Pern Lee''' ({{zh|c=李遠鵬|p=Lǐ Yuǎnpéng}}; born 25 January 1952) is a Taiwanese chemist.

== Early life and education ==
Lee was born on 25 January 1952 in [[Hsinchu, Taiwan]],<ref name="yplcv">{{cite news |title=YUAN-PERN LEE (李遠鵬) |url=https://twas.org/sites/default/files/twas-cv-pub-2015-04_0.pdf |access-date=3 December 2018 |work=The World Academy of Sciences |date=15 September 2015}}</ref> the youngest of painter [[Lee Tze-fan]]'s three sons. He graduated from [[National Taiwan University]] with a bachelor's degree in chemistry and a master's degree in chemistry. He then earned his [[Ph.D.]] in [[applied chemistry]] from the [[University of California, Berkeley]], in 1979.<ref name="nctu">{{cite news |title=Yuan-Pern Lee |url=http://www.ac.nctu.edu.tw/en/member/Yuan-Pern-Lee-20179018 |access-date=3 December 2018 |publisher=National Chiao Tung University}}</ref><ref name="yplcv" />

== Career ==
After receiving his doctorate, Lee began a research career in 1979 at the [[ National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration]] before accepting a teaching position at [[National Tsing Hua University]] in 1981.<ref name="nctu" /><ref name="yplcv" />

Lee was named a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 1999,<ref name="yplcv" /><ref name="nctu" /> and subsequently considered multiple times for membership in the [[Academia Sinica]].<ref name="sinica2004">{{cite news |title=Lee family awaits Academa Sinica membership vote |url=http://www.taipeitimes.com/News/taiwan/archives/2004/07/07/2003178015 |access-date=3 December 2018 |work=Taipei Times |date=7 July 2004}}</ref><ref name="sinicashan">{{cite news |last1=Shan |first1=Shelley |title=Academia Sinica to elect new members today |url=http://www.taipeitimes.com/News/taiwan/archives/2006/07/06/2003317482 |access-date=3 December 2018 |work=Taipei Times |date=6 July 2006}}</ref> Eventually, Yuan-Pern Lee was inducted into Academia Sinica in 2008,<ref name="nctu" /> and the Lees became the first family to have three members serve simultaneously as academicians of Academia Sinica.<ref name="sinicashan" /> Yuan-Pern Lee's induction followed that of his brothers [[Yuan-Chuan Lee]] and [[Yuan T. Lee]].<ref name="sinica2004" /> Yuan-Pern Lee's association with the Academia Sinica began in 1988, when he began working as an adjunct research fellow within the Institute of Atomic and Molecular Sciences.<ref>{{cite news |title=Dr. Yuan-Pern Lee (Chemical Dynamics and Spectroscopy) |url=https://www.iams.sinica.edu.tw/en/?link=member&id=2 |access-date=3 December 2018 |publisher=Academia Sinica |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181204103543/https://www.iams.sinica.edu.tw/en/?link=member&id=2 |archive-date=4 December 2018 |url-status=bot: unknown }}</ref> 

Yuan-Pern Lee has taught at [[National Chiao Tung University]] since 2004 as chair of the Department of Applied Chemistry and director of the Institute of Molecular Science.<ref name="nctu" /><ref name="yplcv" /> Lee was part of a research team at National Chiao Tung University that discovered the [[Criegee intermediate|Criegee intermediate CH2OO]] particle in 2013.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Lee |first1=I-chia |title=University research team finds elusive Criegee molecule |url=http://www.taipeitimes.com/News/taiwan/archives/2013/04/16/2003559875 |access-date=3 December 2018 |work=Taipei Times |date=16 April 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |title= Infrared Absorption Spectrum of the Simplest Criegee Intermediate CH<sub>2</sub>OO |journal= Science |date= 12 April 2013 |volume= 340 |issue= 6129 |pages= 174–176 |doi= 10.1126/science.1234369 |pmid= 23580523 |last1= Su |first1= Yu-Te |last2= Huang |first2= Yu-Hsuan |first3= Witek |last3= Henryk A. |last4= Lee |first4= Yuan-Pern |bibcode = 2013Sci...340..174S |s2cid= 31499893 }}</ref> Lee was a 2017 recipient of the [[Humboldt Research Award]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Dessaul |first1=Arne |title=Resolv gains reinforcement from Taiwan |url=https://news.rub.de/english/2017-04-03-humboldt-research-award-resolv-gains-reinforcement-taiwan |access-date=3 December 2018 |publisher=Ruhr University Bochum |date=3 April 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Prof. Dr. Yuan-Pern Lee |url=https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/pls/web/pub_hn_query.humboldtianer_details?p_lang=en&p_externe_id=2883621 |access-date=3 December 2018 |agency=Humboldt Foundation}}</ref> In 2019, Lee, [[Yuan-Tsong Chen]], and [[Wei Fu-chan]] won Taiwan's {{ill|Presidential Science Prize|zh|總統科學獎}}.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Lin |first1=Chia-nan |title=Three researchers win top prize |url=http://www.taipeitimes.com/News/taiwan/archives/2019/10/30/2003724910 |access-date=30 October 2019 |work=Taipei Times |date=30 October 2019}}</ref>
